text:
marta: Canary rollout of newton-14b (int4) at 10% — seeing intermittent OOMs and p95 latency spikes, tagging ops.
ashwin: saw alerts. here's host log snippet:
```
2024-05-13T09:45:11Z OOM during KV resize (needed 18MB)
slab_free=980 fragmented=47% compaction_runs=0
trace: batch_size=6 max_new_tokens=200 avg_seq=512
```
peter: int4 cuts mem headroom and our KV growth heuristic is too optimistic for long sequences.
sam: quick mitigations: 1) reduce default max_new_tokens to 80 for canary 2) cap batch_size to 3 on long-route 3) enable aggressive slot compactor on canary hosts.
marta: ok applying patch with max_new_tokens=80 and per-route override for /longread. also disabling kv_prefetch for now.
ciara: kicking off evals: perf-eval/1715607890 (int4 vs fp16) longform QA and summarization. quality gate: answer F1 >= -1.0% vs fp16, latency p95 <= +35%.
ops-bot: Canary deploy started: newton-14b-int4-canary -> canary-cluster-7 (deploy id d-8891). Eval job queued.
ashwin: note — slot compactor = aggressive will raise CPU by ~8-12% during warmup. watch CPU and thermal throttling.
sam: also try soft-evict on prefix cache: threshold 0.55 and adaptive-kv-trim on sessions that exceed 300 tokens.
peter: if fragmentation persists, we should consider a short-term fallback to fp16 for routes with average seq_len > 400.
marta: agreed. plan: let canary run 30m with patched params, collect mem fragmentation, p95, and rouge/qa metrics. if OOMs continue -> rollback to fp16 and open a runbook action.
ciara: eval started, will post results here. linking ticket: <http://tracker.internal/RED-11234>
sam: thanks. I'll run a synthetic load with synthetic-long://2000 tokens to validate no KV expand loops.
marta: perfect. will update in ~35m. :eyes:
